newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL rubber ends mostly down, seen falling further.
newsitem.headline: KL rubber ends mostly down, seen falling further.

text.p: Rubber prices extended their losses at the close, with consumers continuing to sideline on expectations of further falls in prices, dealers said.
"Indonesian and Thai prices are still higher than ours. So I feel that the market could drop another 20 percent from current levels," a dealer said.
He added a lack of keen consumer interest also hit prices which also weakened because of the summer holidays which limited European buying.
Activity was mainly from hand-to-mouth basis.
"If prices continue to fall, we may see the INRO five-day average moving nearer to the "may-buy" level which means that INRO may intervene to prop up the market," a trader said.
The five-day moving average was 185.11 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 8 against 187.60 on July 7. The daily indicator price was 181.84 against 182.89.

China was seen in the market. making enquiries in last few days for SMR 20 rubber grade, dealers said. "The Chinese buyers are not very happy with the offered prices and think prices could be cheaper," another dealer said. Suppliers had earlier offered SMR 20 at around 235 cents.
